lessons.rule: Calculate typography font sizes dynamically using ctx.measureText to enforce 75%–85% horizontal canvas occupancy (clamping font size so text width does not exceed 88% canvas width), and anchor placement using ctx.textAlign = 'center' at canvas.width / 2: never allow oversized letters to clip beyond viewport margins or collapse into timid centered blocks with vast negative space.
lessons.why: In build-stamp r1 (score 4.2), the coder scaled up 'BUILD' to fix negative space but failed to center it within safe bounds, completely clipping the letter 'B' off the left side of the screen as 'UILD'.

lessons.rule: Never direct or code a brand resolve or hold as a 100% static freeze: even when holding a logo lockup on a final sustained chord, animate an impact settle on frame 0 (e.g. 4–6 frame stamp slam or ink snap) and maintain continuous micro-motion (such as 12fps boiling paper tooth, halftone grain, or 1.01x camera drift) throughout holds.
lessons.why: In jomiez-lockup (v1: 3.4, r1: 3.9), the director specified 'Nothing moves after the cut: hold... perfectly still for all three beats', resulting in a dead 1.5s freeze that the critic flagged as an unmoving presentation slide.

lessons.rule: Set secondary contact URLs, domain descriptors, and telemetry labels to a minimum font size of 18–22px with wide tracking (+15% to +25%) and high contrast (>= 4.5:1); never render them as sub-14px micro-type or unreadable blurry text.
lessons.why: In S8 (#1 and r1), bottom URLs and metadata labels were rendered as sub-10px hairline micro-type, failing the end-card legibility and pulling scores to 5.6.

lessons.rule: In 3D typography and rotating cylinder setpieces, cull back-facing glyphs (dot product of surface normal and camera vector <= 0 or angle > 90°) to prevent inverted mirror-text from bleeding through, and maintain at least 40px vertical baseline separation between distinct stacked lines.
lessons.why: In software-development (v1: 2.7, film1: 2.4), a hollow rotating 3D cylinder ribbon allowed reversed mirror-lettering from the back of the cylinder to bleed through, overlapping with foreground copy and making the words completely illegible.

lessons.rule: Maintain the film's established art direction and textural system throughout brand resolves; never relapse into generic sci-fi HUD tropes (pitch-black void, thin glowing laser rules, radial lens flares, or corner targeting ticks) when the direction specifies tactile print, editorial broadsheet, or textured paper.
lessons.why: In S7, the coder defaulted to generic radial blur volumetric light rays cutting to an empty pitch-black void, scoring 3.3 and abandoning the established screenprint identity.

lessons.rule: Ensure frame 0 functions immediately as a high-density poster frame: never leave the primary text band or screen center empty for the first 0.5–1.0s. Either detonate high-inertia kinetic slam impacts on frame 0 or populate full-bleed background numerals and architectural registration grids.
lessons.why: In proof-lin-co (3.7) and services-cascade (3.9), layouts held empty cards or static motionless titles for an entire second (1.0s) before any secondary animation or hero typography appeared.

lessons.rule: Animate heavy titles, stamps, and print slabs using a 2–3 frame pullback anticipation (scale ~0.95) followed by steep exponential slam (easeOutQuint/Expo) and an explicit vertical squash-and-rebound on contact (e.g. scaleY: 0.88–0.92, scaleX: 1.08–1.12 settling over 100–150ms); never use uniform scale pops, unstyled cuts, or soft floating opacity fades.
lessons.why: Across build-stamp (v1: 3.1), custom-software (film1: 4.7), and what-we-do-best (r1: 4.7), ink stamp hits and title entrances landed as weak digital pops or sliding fades without the physical squash-and-stretch overshoot requested in the direction.

lessons.rule: Never render generic sci-fi HUD tropes—including thin 1px wireframe perspective floors, corner targeting brackets, laser scanning rules, and floating particle specks—when art direction calls for brutalist, risograph, or print editorial styling. Replace wireframes with heavy structural slabs and replace thin lines with inked rules (>= 8px) or registration bars.
lessons.why: In S5, faint digital plexus lines cluttered the background, and in S6 r1, letterbox crosshairs and thin laser streaks were drawn in a radial void, scoring 3.5 and 4.1.

lessons.rule: When simulating physical squeegee, roller, or ink-drag reveals, drive the incoming element's appearance using a moving canvas ctx.clip() path or textured wipe edge with an explicit leading bar element (e.g. rubber blade or roller cylinder) moving in tandem; never substitute tactile tool sweeps with flat digital opacity fades or unmasked vector slides.
lessons.why: In S5 (#1 and r1), the directed full-frame black squeegee blade was omitted entirely across both attempts, with the coder merely cutting or jittering static text cards, resulting in a 3.5 score.

lessons.rule: When executing a crash-zoom into 3D text geometry for a scene transition, push the camera completely through the glyph's aperture into full-bleed color/black or snap a 90-degree axial cut at peak velocity; never decelerate and stall the camera inside a single clipped, unreadable letter facet.
lessons.why: In hook-slam-prism (4.1 & 4.6) and cylinder-vortex (2.8), the camera pushed linearly into letters ('W' and 'SOFTWARE') and froze on unreadable cropped white polygons and empty horizon gaps.

lessons.rule: When wrapping multi-tier kinetic type around a 3D cylindrical surface or curved ribbon, assign explicit vertical Y-axis offsets (e.g. -240px, 0px, +240px) and expand the cylinder radius (R >= 650px) to prevent distinct counter-rotating typographic tiers from colliding into an illegible tangle.
lessons.why: In cylinder-vortex (2.8), all three text tiers ('WEBSITES', 'AI SYSTEMS', 'SAAS PRODUCTS') were rendered along the same horizontal plane, colliding directly on top of each other and resulting in only 31% frame coverage.

lessons.rule: Drive kinetic typography from a keyed array of state objects `[{t, text, color, glowRadius}]` and render strictly the state matching the current timestamp; never clump multiple sequential phrases into a single static string or skip directed intermediate word beats.
lessons.why: In Scene 1 (score 5.5) and Scene 7 (score 4.8), the coder rendered 'lacking Ideas for your' as a single clumped string rather than stepping every 0.25 s, and skipped intermediate hits ('Find it', 'Pin it', 'Get Inspired'), causing long static holds.

lessons.rule: When positioning flanking modular slabs, auxiliary UI containers, or twin sub-labels around central typography, calculate bounds using ctx.measureText and enforce an explicit clearance of at least 80–120px outside the text boundaries to prevent occlusion or character overlaps.
lessons.why: In custom-software-foundry (r2) and neural-synthesis (#1, #2), flanking modular plates occluded outer letterforms ('S' and 'E' of 'CUSTOM SOFTWARE') and twin 'INTELLIGENT SYSTEMS' boxes collided with overlapping characters, dropping scores to 3.7–4.7.

lessons.rule: When executing a crash zoom into an interior glyph counter (such as the bowl of an 'O') for an iris match-cut, measure the target glyph's bounding center using ctx.measureText metrics and anchor ctx.translate(glyphCenterX, glyphCenterY) directly on that point before scaling; never scale from the canvas origin or word center.
lessons.why: In iris-client-signature (scores 3.7–5.5), the camera zoom anchored off-center towards the ampersand and 'C', causing a jarring spatial mismatch when cutting to the concentric mechanical iris.

lessons.rule: In print, risograph, and ink press art directions, render geometry and text as flat graphic plates, multi-pass ink misregistrations, or high-contrast silhouette cuts; never shade elements with Phong specular highlights, rounded plastic 3D bevels, or metallic gradient spheres.
lessons.why: In S1, S2, and S4, the coder rendered 3D beveled letters, clay-like shaded spheres, and reflective metallic brown cylinders, producing a dated 2000s slot-machine look that scored 3.0–4.8.

lessons.rule: Never use horizontal digital glitch slice displacements or Photoshop-style jagged torn-paper banners when art direction specifies physical press mechanics; reveal or deform typography using continuous tool wipes (squeegees, rollers), fluid bleeds, or physical plate stamps.
lessons.why: In S1 and S8, the coder sliced horizontal seams through hero type like a cyberpunk glitch, and in S2 used a faux torn-paper banner, destroying the screenprint aesthetic.

lessons.rule: Do not enclose secondary metadata, category tags, or sub-labels in rounded rectangular 'pill' button containers. Render technical tags as uncontained uppercase monospace typography with wide tracking (+20% to +35%) anchored directly along datum baselines or fine hairline bracket crosshairs.
lessons.why: In proven-execution (#1, #2, r1, r2, film1), the coder repeatedly rendered 'WEBSITE DESIGN' and 'MOBILE APPS' inside rounded web UI button pills, keeping scores suppressed between 4.6 and 5.5 until forced to strip them out for clean monospace typography.

lessons.rule: When executing paper louvers, shearing bands, or directional wipes between beats, render incoming elements directly onto the moving panels or initiate incoming motion before the outgoing panels exit; never leave the canvas as a bare background for 100–300ms during transition splits.
lessons.why: In riso-impact-hook and halftone-matrix-engine, horizontal louvers and wipes cleared the screen completely, leaving 00:00.750–00:00.910 as a dead blank canvas before the next text layer entered.

lessons.rule: When animating text or logo disintegration into particles that reassemble, store each particle's home anchor (targetX, targetY) sampled from the glyph geometry; disperse them outward during the burst phase, then interpolate (lerp) each particle strictly back to its home anchor before the reform beat rather than letting particles drift unboundedly off-screen or collapse into an arbitrary point.
lessons.why: In ai-development (v1: 3.8, r1: 3.7), the coder first collapsed text into a single center dot, then replaced it with drifting polygonal shards that floated off into empty space without ever reforming the text as directed.

lessons.rule: Execute expanding shockwave scene transitions using an expanding circular clipping path (arc scaling from 0% to 250% frame width with easeOutExpo) and additive radial bloom; never abruptly fill the entire canvas with solid background color or display incoming UI elements prior to the wave edge.
lessons.why: In Scene 2, the coder jumped abruptly to a solid red screen containing a full four-card UI grid at 1.17 s rather than expanding a circular blast wave on the white canvas to reveal the UI beneath.

lessons.rule: Simulate risograph or print ink overprinting using ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'multiply' on light backgrounds (or 'screen' on dark backgrounds) with deliberate 4–12px misregistration offsets between plates; never approximate print separation using opaque stacked drop-shadows or faux-extruded 3D bevels.
lessons.why: In overprint-color-split, attempts scored 2.7–4.4 because the coder drew faux-extruded 3D drop shadows and opaque color blocks rather than authentic multiply blend overprinting.

lessons.rule: When revealing text via canvas clip() paths or directional wipe masks, pad the clipping bounds by at least 15–20% beyond measured font height and string width to avoid truncating ascenders, descenders, and outer letterform strokes.
lessons.why: In modular-scale (#1, #2), wipe masks clipped both 'PRODUCTS' and 'WORLDWIDE' awkwardly throughout the intro and freeze hold, dragging scene scores down to 4.5.

lessons.rule: When animating sequential text lines into a multi-tier column stack, compute each tier's final baseline position prior to entrance and animate preceding lines to their target positions using an easing curve triggered on the exact impact frame of each incoming tier; never stamp an incoming line directly over an existing line.
lessons.why: In halftone-matrix-engine, 'SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT' slammed directly on top of 'WEBSITE DESIGN' at 00:01.000 in an illegible collision before abruptly shifting down.

lessons.rule: Cleanse all auxiliary UI elements, lingering action buttons, and cursor paths on frame 0 (t = 0.00s) of every new shot unless explicitly logged in the reference; never leave orphan buttons or cursor sprites floating from the preceding scene during transition morphs.
lessons.why: In Scene 6 (score 4.4 -> 4.9), residual share buttons and cursor graphics lingered on frame 0 during the red pill button expansion, cluttering the opening frame.

lessons.rule: When simulating search input changes, animate previous text clearing letter-by-letter (40–60ms/char) or via rapid selection wipe, pause 1–2 beats with a blinking caret, and type new characters sequentially at 50–80ms intervals; never vanish the string instantaneously and stall on a dead static bar for >0.5s.
lessons.why: In Scene 3 (score 4.8 -> 5.0), 'Search' vanished instantaneously at 1.7 s, leaving a 1.33 s dead freeze before 'Ui animations' abruptly appeared, dragging down rhythm and motion scores.

lessons.rule: Compute all transition triggers, visual impacts, and scene cuts using strict musical beat quantization (e.g. Math.round(t / beatDuration) * beatDuration or explicit beat-index helpers); never hardcode arbitrary floating-point seconds that drift 30–50ms off the 16th-note tempo grid.
lessons.why: In S2, S4, and S5, hardcoded cutoffs (such as 0.533s, 2.033s, and 2.05s instead of 0.500s and 2.000s at 120 BPM) broke downbeat synchronization and degraded rhythm scores down to 2–4.

lessons.rule: When animating a cursive lettermark or logo draw-on, render the path using ctx.setLineDash([length, length]) and animate ctx.lineDashOffset from length down to 0 over the specified beat duration; never substitute path reveals with an instantaneous cut to a static icon badge or flat color fill.
lessons.why: In Scene 2 (score 2.8 -> 4.9), the coder failed to draw the Pinterest cursive 'P' monogram path vertically, jumping straight to a flat red screen and a generic motionless badge.

lessons.rule: When scene direction specifies an exit transition or breath hold on the final beat (e.g. a color sweep, sheet wipe, or camera dive before the cut), verify the scene duration spans all directed beats and code the transition logic explicitly for that final beat; never stop animation logic at the hero text resolve and let the scene stall or cut out prematurely.
lessons.why: In what-we-do-best (v1: 5.0, r1: 4.7, film1: 5.8), across all three versions the coder animated the word reveals ('WHAT', 'WE DO', 'BEST') but omitted Beat 37's full-bleed sheet sweep and central ink-pool hold, leaving the scene hanging statically before the brand cut.

lessons.rule: Constrain text backlights and UI glow halos to a radius of 1.2x–1.5x the text cap-height (150–250px) using high-saturation hex values (`#FF1A35`, `#E60023`) and exponential decay; never flood the canvas with wide 800px diffuse gradients that wash out into pale pink or magenta fields.
lessons.why: In Scenes 1 and 7, red backlight flares were rendered as expansive, desaturated pink washes across the entire screen instead of punchy, saturated radial blooms concentrated behind the active words.

lessons.rule: When choreographing a rhythmic transition where typography condenses into a focal core, compress letterforms using geometric slicing masks or converging shard bands into a radiant graphic mark (>= 180–240px) with screen shake; never shrink the entire layout uniformly into a tiny 40px icon floating in an empty void.
lessons.why: In proof-lin-co (3.7 & 4.9), the coder lazily scaled the entire scene down into a tiny 40px glowing diamond floating lost in an empty black void.

lessons.rule: Drive interactive hand/pointer cursors along continuous Bezier paths without stationary pauses exceeding 0.2s; on click contact, apply a 2-frame scale squeeze (scale: 0.90) followed by popping the selected card forward (scale: 1.15x–1.35x, drop-shadow blur: 40–60px) while blurring background cards with ctx.filter = 'blur(12px)'.
lessons.why: In Scene 4 and Scene 5 (scores 4.1 and 4.6), the cursor froze stationary for 1.0–1.33 seconds and the hero card selection failed to elevate in z-space or apply depth blur to the surrounding grid.

lessons.rule: Simulate viscous liquid drops, ink splatters, and melting letterforms using thresholded blur compositing (e.g. drawing circular clusters through ctx.filter = 'blur(16px) contrast(30)' on an offscreen canvas); never substitute wet ink with dry point particles, scratch lines, or static vector stamps.
lessons.why: In S1, S2, and S8, the coder repeatedly relied on thin wireframe scratch debris, static grunge stamps, or generic radial particle swarms, failing the directed wet ink fluid simulation.
